source.section: PDF p10 Line 4 'What pensions are exempt?' first bullet (contributory pension of the U.S. Government); Tax Treatment of Government Pensions, 'Federal employee contributory pension'; Form 1 lines 2a, 2c, 4, 10-22; tax table PDF p38

worked: Federal AGI = U.S. civil service (federal contributory) pension 50,000.00 (person 0) + private pension 30,000.00 (person 1) = 80,000.00 (given). Federal taxable income = 80,000.00 - 34,700.00 standard deduction (31,500.00 + 2 x 1,600.00 age 65 or older) = 45,300.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Massachusetts Form 1 (the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt items): Line 4 taxable pensions = 0.00 for the 50,000.00 U.S. civil service (federal contributory) pension (exempt: contributory pension of the U.S. Government, PDF p10 first bullet) + 30,000.00 private pension (taxed: most private pensions are taxable, PDF p10) = 30,000.00. Line 10 total 5.0% income = 30,000.00. Line 16 total deductions = 0.00. Line 17 = 30,000.00 - 0.00 = 30,000.00. Line 2a personal exemption (married_joint) = 8,800.00; line 2c age 65 or over before 2026: 2 x 700.00 = 1,400.00; line 2g = line 18 = 10,200.00. Line 19 = 30,000.00 - 10,200.00 = 19,800.00. Line 20 interest and dividends = 0.00. Line 21 = 19,800.00. Line 22 = 19,800.00 x 0.05 = 990.00 (line 21 is under 24,000, so the form uses the tax table, PDF p38: the table gives 991). No 8.5%/12% income or long-term gains (lines 23-24 = 0.00); 4% surtax 0.00 (line 21 is under 1,083,150). Line 28 total tax = 990.00; no credits (No Tax Status and the Limited Income Credit do not apply: Massachusetts AGI 30,000.00 is over their limits). State income tax = 990.00.
